_comment: Copy to <repo>/spawn.json and edit. Start it with: firecode spawn-server
Then give a guest access to it with: firecode claude --host-port 9770 ...
Projects are named keys on purpose. The caller picks a name, never a
path, so an agent in a VM cannot ask for a directory you did not list.
Datasets are disks handed to a VM whole - nothing is copied, so a 5TB
volume attaches as fast as a small one. Named, like projects, so an agent
asks for 'tpcc' and never for a device. Give a SNAPSHOT, not the live
volume: writes then land in copy-on-write space and the original is
untouched, which is what makes rw safe. A database needs rw to start.

tpcc.note: 5TB TPCC, snapshot of /dev/vg/tpcc - point the server's -D at the mountpoint
